author: Rahul kp
title: Target Costing
simple_words: Start with the price customers will pay, deduct the profit you want, and make the product within the cost left.

definitions.meaning: A cost management tool where the allowable cost is fixed as market price minus desired profit, before the product is designed and made.
definitions.note: Cost is an input, not a result!

definitions.meaning: The excess of the current estimated cost of the product over its target cost. It must be closed by value engineering and cost reduction.
definitions.note: Gap exists only if estimate > target

key_points: Market-driven: ==target selling price== comes from customers and competitors
Used at the design and planning stage, not after production starts
Cost reduction is done by ==value engineering== and team effort of design, production and marketing
Traditional costing: Cost + Profit = Price. Target costing reverses it
formula_hook: price down, profit down, cost left

formulas.name: Target Cost
formulas.legend: TSP = target selling price per unit; TP = target profit per unit

formulas.name: Target Profit (margin on sales)
formulas.legend: m = desired profit as a fraction of sales price. Use only if the margin is given on sales.

formulas.name: Cost Gap
formulas.legend: EC = current estimated cost per unit. Positive gap means cost must be cut.

insight.punchline: Price is fixed, cost must bend!
insight.text: In target costing the market sets the price, so profit is protected only by cutting cost, not by raising price.

memory_trick.explanation: Think of a thali budget: the restaurant fixes the thali price, keeps its profit aside, and the cook gets only the permitted cost for ingredients.

exam_tip: Read whether the profit is on sales or on cost or on investment. Then compute target profit before target cost.

doubt.question: Is the cost gap always a loss?
doubt.answer: No. It is not a loss yet. It is the cost reduction still needed to earn the target profit. If the gap is zero or negative, the target is met.

mistakes.right: Target cost = Target selling price − Target profit

mistakes.wrong: Taking profit margin on cost when the question says on sales
mistakes.right: Apply the given base: !!on sales!! means percentage of selling price

mistakes.wrong: Cost gap = Target cost − Estimated cost
mistakes.right: Cost gap = Estimated cost − Target cost

mistakes.wrong: Raising the price to close the gap
mistakes.right: Price is set by the market; close the gap through value engineering and cost cuts
